html:
The global order is being significantly shaped today by escalating threats of conflict surrounding Iran and a discernible shift in US foreign policy towards the Ukraine war. US and Israeli officials threaten renewed strikes against Iran, prompting strong warnings of retaliation from Tehran, while incidents in the Strait of Hormuz underscore rising tensions. Concurrently, US support for Ukraine appears to be evolving, with President Trump making Russia-friendly moves and pressing Kyiv to settle the conflict.

US-Ukraine-Russia: Despite a resumption of US intelligence sharing with Ukraine, which Ukrainian leader Zelensky said "works now," tensions persist regarding overall US policy. Zelensky and President Trump appear at loggerheads, with President Trump actively seeking a way to end the war with Ukraine through Russia-friendly actions. His envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russians. Russia's foreign minister, Lavrov, stated that Russia would not make political concessions but is open to resuming relations with the West. Reports also note North Korean workers are at a Russian drone factory, raising concerns over Pyongyang gaining knowledge of advanced weapons.

Middle East Security: The Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint, with Iran’s IRGC claiming mines halted two tankers and downed a US MQ-9 drone. Iranian President Pezeshkian warned a new US war would bring "destruction and damage" to the entire Middle East, while Iran's foreign minister stated Russia and Iran have "never" worked so closely. US Secretary of Defense Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, with Iran being the primary topic, ahead of Israel's October 27 elections. President Trump has given Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu his "complete and total endorsement," while US Vice President JD Vance declined to endorse Netanyahu, focusing instead on American candidates. Regionally, Sudan saw drone strikes kill more than 300 people in a market and at a funeral, and a Houthi missile strike in Yemen killed 73 security recruits. The United Kingdom will deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.

Global Economy & US Politics: President Trump faces a lawsuit over Canadian tariffs, accused of exceeding authority and harming American businesses. Amidst upcoming midterm elections, President Trump plans to spend $400 million to support Republicans and has announced an anti-fraud incentive program, suggesting he could be its "arbitrator." United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby's call for a US wealth tax has drawn a rightwing backlash. In a positive economic note, the US Federal Aviation Administration certified Boeing's 737 Max 10, years after its maiden flight.

European Unrest: France is grappling with significant internal unrest, marked by recent rioting and demonstrations. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu vowed a "massive" police deployment for new protests, while Italy approved deploying 500 troops to Milan following violent clashes and fuel price protests that impacted food deliveries. Meanwhile, Greece rejected Libya's approval of a maritime border demarcation agreement with Turkey, which the Libyan Parliament had recently approved, ending a six-year boycott.

Other Global Developments: In Canada, voters in Alberta overwhelmingly rejected a bid for separatism, a "great result" for Canada, according to Prime Minister Carney. Africa is facing a spreading Ebola outbreak, with Nigeria confirming its first case in Abuja, following Kenya's earlier infections. In Brazil, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign is seeking to disqualify Flavio Bolsonaro from the presidential runoff election, alleging social media interference, as polls show the candidates virtually tied.
